Test Case Description: Verify Client Approval module loads successfully
Preconditions: User is authenticated and has access to Client Approval (Module ID 6961)
Test Steps:
1. Log in to KAIRO
2. Navigate to Identities > Client Approval
3. Wait for the page to load completely
Expected Result: Page loads without errors. Filter Criteria section
Actual Result: Pending Approvals section and Status Reasons section are all visible. No JavaScript errors in console.

Test Case Description: Verify initial action button states on load
Preconditions: Client Approval module is loaded
Test Steps:
1. Observe the action panel buttons (View / Approve / Reject / Cancel)
2. Note the enabled/disabled state of each button
Expected Result: View, Approve and Reject buttons are disabled. Cancel button is enabled. No client is selected.

Test Case Description: Verify module ID is correctly set to 6961
Preconditions: Client Approval module is loaded
Test Steps:
1. Inspect the hidden field #moduleId in the DOM (browser DevTools)
2. Confirm its value
Expected Result: Hidden field #moduleId has value '6961'.

Test Case Description: Verify default branch is auto-populated from session
Preconditions: Client Approval module is loaded, user session contains a valid OurBranchID
Test Steps:
1. Observe the Branch ID field (#txt_branchId) on page load
2. Observe the branch hidden field (#txt_branchIdValue)
3. Observe the branch name label (#spn_branchName)
Expected Result: #txt_branchId is pre-filled with the session branch ID. #txt_branchIdValue holds the branch ID. #spn_branchName shows the branch name from session.

Test Case Description: Verify hidden fields for default branch are present in DOM
Preconditions: Client Approval module is loaded
Test Steps:
1. Open browser DevTools
2. Inspect for #hdn_defaultBranchId and #hdn_defaultBranchName elements
Expected Result: Both hidden fields exist and contain the server-side default branch ID and name respectively.

Test Case Description: Verify Client Type dropdown is populated from server
Preconditions: Client Approval module is loaded
Test Steps:
1. Click the Client Type dropdown (#ddl_clientType)
2. Observe the available options
Expected Result: Dropdown is populated with client type options loaded server-side via ViewData['ClientTypeOptions']. A default placeholder 'Select Type' is shown.

Test Case Description: Verify Filter Criteria section can be collapsed and expanded
Preconditions: Client Approval module is loaded
Test Steps:
1. Click the toggle button (#btn_toggleFilters) on the Filter Criteria section header
2. Observe the section content
3. Click the toggle button again
Expected Result: Section collapses on first click (content hidden). Section expands on second click (content visible). Toggle icon changes accordingly.

Test Case Description: Verify Branch ID search button opens branch search modal
Preconditions: Client Approval module is loaded
Test Steps:
1. Click the search icon button (#btn_searchBranch) next to the Branch ID field
2. Observe the modal or search panel
Expected Result: A branch search modal opens allowing the user to search and select a branch.

Test Case Description: Verify selecting a branch via search modal updates the Branch ID field
Preconditions: Branch search modal is open
Test Steps:
1. Search for and double-click or select a valid branch in the modal
2. Observe the Branch ID field and branch name label
Expected Result: #txt_branchId is updated with the selected branch code/ID. #txt_branchIdValue is updated with the branch ID. #spn_branchName shows the selected branch name.

Test Case Description: Verify Application ID search button is disabled when no Client Type is selected
Preconditions: Client Approval module is loaded and Client Type dropdown shows placeholder
Test Steps:
1. Ensure no Client Type is selected (value is empty)
2. Observe the Application ID search button (#btn_searchApplication) state
Expected Result: #btn_searchApplication is disabled and cannot be clicked.

Test Case Description: Verify Application ID search button is enabled when Client Type is selected
Preconditions: Client Approval module is loaded
Test Steps:
1. Select any Client Type from #ddl_clientType
2. Observe the Application ID search button (#btn_searchApplication) state
Expected Result: #btn_searchApplication becomes enabled and is clickable.

Test Case Description: Verify Application ID search button opens application search modal
Preconditions: Client Approval module is loaded, Client Type is selected
Test Steps:
1. Select a Client Type
2. Click #btn_searchApplication
Expected Result: Application search modal opens. Available applications are filtered according to the selected branch and client type.

Test Case Description: Verify selecting an application via search modal updates the Application ID field
Preconditions: Application search modal is open with results
Test Steps:
1. Select/double-click a valid application in the modal
2. Observe the Application ID field and label
Expected Result: #txt_applicationId is updated with the selected application ID. #txt_applicationIdValue holds the raw ID. #spn_applicationName shows the application name.

Test Case Description: Verify Application ID field clears when Client Type is changed
Preconditions: Application ID field is populated, Client Type is changed
Test Steps:
1. Select a Client Type and select an Application ID
2. Change the Client Type to a different value
3. Observe the Application ID field
Expected Result: Application ID field (#txt_applicationId) is cleared. #txt_applicationIdValue is empty. #spn_applicationName is cleared.

Test Case Description: Verify Client Type change auto-loads Status Reasons table

Test Case Description: Verify record count badge updates after loading
Preconditions: Load Approvals clicked and records are returned

Test Case Description: Verify Pending Approvals section can be collapsed and expanded

Test Steps:

2. Observe the View button (#btn_view) state
Expected Result: View button is enabled. Approve and Reject buttons are also enabled.

Test Case Description: Verify selecting two or more clients disables View button

Test Steps:
1. Check two or more .ca-client-checkbox rows
2. Observe the View button (#btn_view) state

Test Steps:
1. Click #chk_selectAll again to deselect
2. Observe all row checkboxes

Test Case Description: Verify Select All checkbox state when individual rows are manually checked/unchecked

2. Uncheck one individual .ca-client-checkbox

Test Case Description: Verify View button remains disabled when no client is selected

2. Attempt to click View button
Expected Result: View button (#btn_view) is disabled and does not respond to click. No message is shown.

Test Case Description: Verify View button is disabled when multiple clients are selected

2. Observe View button state
Expected Result: View button is disabled.

Test Case Description: Verify Status Reasons section is visible

Test Case Description: Verify Status Reasons table populates based on Client Type selection

Test Case Description: Verify Status Reasons section can be collapsed and expanded
Preconditions: Client Approval module is loaded and Status Reasons section is visible
Test Steps:
1. Click the toggle button (#btn_toggleStatusReasons)
2. Observe the section
3. Click again

Test Case Description: Verify Approve button shows SweetAlert confirmation dialog
Preconditions: One or more clients are selected via .ca-client-checkbox
Test Steps:
1. Select at least one client in the approval table
2. Click #btn_approve
Expected Result: A SweetAlert confirmation dialog appears showing the number of clients about to be approved. Dialog has Confirm and Cancel options.

Test Case Description: Verify SweetAlert shows correct client count for approval
Preconditions: Multiple clients are selected
Test Steps:
1. Select 3 clients
2. Click #btn_approve
3. Read the SweetAlert message
Expected Result: SweetAlert message shows '3' (or the selected count) in the confirmation prompt.

Test Case Description: Verify cancelling the SweetAlert does not submit approval
Preconditions: SweetAlert approval confirmation dialog is open
Test Steps:
1. Click Cancel (or press Escape) on the SweetAlert dialog
2. Observe the network requests and table state
Expected Result: No request is sent to approve-clients. Table selection is unchanged.

Test Case Description: Verify confirming approval calls approve-clients endpoint
Preconditions: One or more clients are selected, SweetAlert is open
Test Steps:
1. Select clients
2. Click #btn_approve
3. Click Confirm on SweetAlert dialog
Expected Result: A POST request is made to Identities/ClientApproval/approve-clients with OurBranchID, ApprovedBy, ApprovedOn, and DetailRecords (XML) in the payload.

Test Case Description: Verify approve-clients request includes correct XML payload (DetailRecords)
Preconditions: Clients are selected and approval is confirmed
Test Steps:
1. Open browser DevTools Network tab
2. Select clients and confirm approval
3. Inspect the POST body of approve-clients
Expected Result: DetailRecords field contains valid XML with one <dt_ClientApproval> (or equivalent) element per selected client. Each element contains the client's identifier.

Test Case Description: Verify approve-clients request includes OurBranchID from session
Preconditions: User session has a valid OurBranchID, approval is confirmed
Test Steps:
1. Confirm approval
2. Inspect the POST body of approve-clients
Expected Result: OurBranchID in the payload matches the branch from the user's session context.

Test Case Description: Verify approve-clients request includes ApprovedBy from session
Preconditions: Approval is confirmed
Test Steps:
1. Confirm approval
2. Inspect the POST body of approve-clients
Expected Result: ApprovedBy in the payload matches the logged-in operator/user ID.

Test Case Description: Verify addClientSupervisionData is called after successful approval
Preconditions: Approval is confirmed and approve-clients returns success
Test Steps:
1. Confirm approval and monitor network requests
2. Observe requests after the approve-clients call returns
Expected Result: A POST request is made to Identities/ClientApproval/add-client-supervision-data for the approved clients as an audit trail.

Test Case Description: Verify success message is shown after approval
Preconditions: Approval is confirmed and the API returns success
Test Steps:
1. Select clients and confirm approval
2. Observe the message panel (#dv_messagePanel)
Expected Result: #dv_messagePanel shows a success message confirming the clients were approved. Message icon is success style.

Test Case Description: Verify selected clients are cleared after successful approval
Preconditions: Approval is confirmed and the API returns success
Test Steps:
1. Select clients and confirm approval
2. Observe the approval table
Expected Result: Previously checked checkboxes are unchecked. #chk_selectAll is unchecked. selectedClients array is empty. View, Approve and Reject buttons return to disabled state.

Test Case Description: Verify Approve button is disabled when no client is selected
Preconditions: Pending Approvals table is loaded and no row is checked
Test Steps:
1. Confirm no checkboxes are checked
2. Observe #btn_approve state
Expected Result: #btn_approve is disabled.

Test Case Description: Verify Reject button opens rejection modal when clients are selected
Preconditions: One or more clients are selected
Test Steps:
1. Select at least one client
2. Click #btn_reject
Expected Result: The rejection modal (#mdl_rejection) opens. The #spn_rejectionCount shows the number of selected clients. #txa_rejectionRemarks is empty.

Test Case Description: Verify rejection modal shows correct selected client count
Preconditions: Two clients are selected, rejection modal is open
Test Steps:
1. Select 2 clients
2. Click #btn_reject
3. Read the count in the modal alert (#spn_rejectionCount)
Expected Result: #spn_rejectionCount displays '2'.

Test Case Description: Verify rejection remarks textarea is cleared each time rejection modal opens
Preconditions: Rejection modal was previously used with text
Test Steps:
1. Submit a rejection (or cancel it)
2. Re-select clients and click #btn_reject again
3. Observe #txa_rejectionRemarks
Expected Result: #txa_rejectionRemarks is empty / cleared when the modal opens.

Test Case Description: Verify rejection form validation fails when remarks are empty
Preconditions: Rejection modal is open, #txa_rejectionRemarks is empty
Test Steps:
1. Leave #txa_rejectionRemarks empty
2. Click #btn_confirmReject
Expected Result: Form does not submit. Validation error message appears. The field highlights as invalid (.is-invalid or HTML5 native).

Test Case Description: Verify rejection form validation fails when remarks are fewer than 10 characters
Preconditions: Rejection modal is open
Test Steps:
1. Type fewer than 10 characters in #txa_rejectionRemarks (e.g. 'short')
2. Click #btn_confirmReject
Expected Result: Form does not submit. Validation error message appears: 'Please provide a valid rejection reason (minimum 10 characters)'.

Test Case Description: Verify rejection form validation passes with 10 or more characters
Preconditions: Rejection modal is open
Test Steps:
1. Type 10 or more characters in #txa_rejectionRemarks (e.g. 'Valid long reason')
2. Click #btn_confirmReject
Expected Result: Form passes HTML5 validation. Rejection is submitted.

Test Case Description: Verify confirming rejection calls reject-clients endpoint
Preconditions: Rejection modal is open with valid remarks
Test Steps:
1. Enter valid remarks (10+ chars)
2. Click #btn_confirmReject
Expected Result: A POST request is made to Identities/ClientApproval/reject-clients with OurBranchID, RejectedReason, RejectedBy, and DetailRecords (XML) in the payload.

Test Case Description: Verify reject-clients request includes correct XML payload (DetailRecords)
Preconditions: Rejection is confirmed
Test Steps:
1. Enter valid remarks and confirm rejection
2. Inspect the POST body of reject-clients in DevTools
Expected Result: DetailRecords field contains valid XML with an element per selected client.

Test Case Description: Verify reject-clients request includes RejectedReason matching typed remarks

Test Case Description: Verify reject-clients request includes RejectedBy from session
Preconditions: Rejection is confirmed
Test Steps:
1. Confirm rejection
2. Inspect the POST body
Expected Result: RejectedBy in the payload matches the logged-in operator/user ID.

Test Case Description: Verify success message is shown after successful rejection

Test Steps:
1. Enter valid remarks and confirm rejection
2. Observe the message panel
Expected Result: #dv_messagePanel shows a success message indicating clients were rejected.

Test Case Description: Verify rejection modal closes after successful rejection

Test Steps:

Test Case Description: Verify Cancel / Close button clears the pending approvals table
Preconditions: Pending Approvals table has records and optionally some are selected

2. Observe the table body
Expected Result: #tbl_approvalBody is cleared to the 'No records to display.' placeholder row.

Test Case Description: Verify Cancel button resets the selectedClients array
Preconditions: One or more clients are selected in the table
Test Steps:

3. Observe action button states

Test Steps: 1. Click the Refresh button in the window header (data-action='refresh')
Expected Result: The module reloads. Filters reset to defaults. Table is cleared.

Test Case Description: Verify unauthenticated user is redirected to login

Test Steps: 1. Open the Client Approval URL directly (Identities/ClientApproval) without a valid session
Expected Result: User is redirected to the login page. No module content is shown.

Test Case Description: Verify XSRF token is included in all POST requests

Test Steps:
1. Open DevTools Network
2. Trigger any POST action (load approvals, approve, reject)
Expected Result: All POST requests include the anti-forgery (X-XSRF-TOKEN or __RequestVerificationToken) header or form field.

Test Case Description: Verify unauthorized user cannot access Client Approval module

2. Navigate to Identities/ClientApproval

Test Steps:

2. Select clients and confirm approval
Expected Result: Error message is shown to the user. Selected clients remain checked (selection not cleared). User can retry.

Test Case Description: Verify error handling when reject-clients returns 500
Preconditions: Server error on reject-clients endpoint
Test Steps:
1. Simulate a server error on reject-clients
2. Enter remarks and confirm rejection
Expected Result: Error message is shown. Rejection modal may stay open. No data is corrupted.

Test Case Description: Verify error handling when get-status-reasons returns empty or error

2. Observe the Status Reasons table
Expected Result: Table shows 'No records to display.' placeholder. No JavaScript error in console.
